readings.title: Words Beyond the Yardĕn
readings.subtitle: The Command to Possess
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 1:1] These are the words which Mosheh spoke to all Yisra’ĕl beyond the Yardĕn in the wilderness, in the desert plain opposite Suph, between Paran and Tophel, and Laḇan, and Ḥatsĕroth, and Di Zahaḇ, [2] eleven days from Ḥorĕḇ by way of Mount Sĕ’ir to Qaḏĕsh Barnĕa. [3] And it came to be in the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, that Mosheh spoke to the children of Yisra’ĕl according to all that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded him to say to them, [4] after he had smitten Siḥon sovereign of the Amorites, who dwelt in Ḥeshbon, and Og̱ sovereign of Bashan, who dwelt at Ashtaroth in Edre’i. [5] Beyond the Yardĕn in the land of Mo’aḇ, Mosheh undertook to declare this Torah, saying, [6] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> spoke to us in Ḥorĕḇ, saying, <dq>‘You have dwelt long enough at this mountain.</dq> [7] <dq>‘Turn and take your journey, and go to the mountains of the Amorites, and to all the neighbouring places in the desert plain, in the mountains and in the low country, and in the South and on the seacoast, to the land of the Kena’anites and to Leḇanon, as far as the great river, the River Euphrates.</dq> [8] <dq>‘See, <dn>I</dn> have set the land before you. Go in and possess the land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> swore to your fathers, to Aḇraham, to Yitsḥaq, and to Ya’aqoḇ, to give to them and their seed after them.’</dq>”

readings.title: Appointing the Administration
readings.subtitle: Wisdom in Leadership
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 1:9] “And I spoke to you at that time, saying, ‘I am unable to bear you by myself. [10] ‘<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has increased you, and see, you are today as the stars of the heavens for plenty. [11] ‘<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of your fathers is going to add to you a thousand times more than you are, and bless you as <dn>He</dn> has promised you! [12] ‘How do I bear your pressure and your burden and your strife by myself? [13] ‘Choose wise and understanding men, known to your tribes, and let me appoint them as your heads.’ [14] “And you answered me and said, ‘The word which you have spoken to us to do is good.’ [15] “And I took the heads of your tribes, wise and known men, and made them heads over you, leaders of thousands, and leaders of hundreds, and leaders of fifties, and leaders of tens, and officers for your tribes. [16] “And I commanded your judges at that time, saying, ‘Hear the cases between your brothers, and judge righteously between a man and his brother or the stranger who is with him. [17] ‘Do not show partiality in right-ruling, hear the small as well as the great. Do not fear any man’s face, for the right-ruling is <dn>Elohim</dn>’s. And the case which is too hard for you, bring it to me, and I shall hear it.’ [18] “And I commanded you at that time all the words which you should do.”

readings.title: The Reconnaissance
readings.subtitle: The Report of the Twelve
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 1:19] “Then we departed from Ḥorĕḇ, and went through all that great and awesome wilderness which you saw on the way to the mountains of the Amorites, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> had commanded us. And we came to Qaḏĕsh Barnĕa. [20] “And I said to you, ‘You have come to the mountains of the Amorites, which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving us. [21] ‘See, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has set the land before you. Go up and possess it, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of your fathers has spoken to you. Do not fear, nor be discouraged.’ [22] “And all of you came near to me and said, ‘Let us send men before us, and let them search out the land for us, and bring back word to us of the way by which we should go up, and of the cities into which we would come.’ [23] “And the matter was good in my eyes, so I took twelve men of you, one man from each tribe. [24] “And they turned and went up into the mountains, and came to the wadi Eshkol, and spied it out. [25] “And they took some of the fruit of the land in their hands and brought it down to us, and brought back word to us, saying, ‘The land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving us is good.’ ”

readings.title: The Rebellion at Qaḏĕsh
readings.subtitle: Unbelief and Consequence
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 1:26] “But you would not go up, and rebelled against the mouth of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. [27] “And you grumbled in your tents, and said, ‘Because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was hating us, <dn>He</dn> has brought us out of the land of Mitsrayim, to give us into the hand of the Amorites, to destroy us. [28] ‘Where are we going? Our brothers have discouraged our hearts, saying, “The people are greater and taller than we, the cities are great and walled up to the heavens, and we saw the sons of the Anaqim there too.” ’ [29] “Then I said to you, ‘Have no dread or fear of them. [30] ‘<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, who goes before you, <dn>He</dn> does fight for you, according to all <dn>He</dn> did for you in Mitsrayim before your eyes, [31] ‘and in the wilderness, where you saw how <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has carried you, as a man carries his son, in all the way that you went until you came to this place.’ [32] “Yet of this matter you did not believe <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, [33] who went in the way before you to search out a place for you to pitch your tents, to show you by fire by night which way you should go, and in the cloud by day. [34] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> heard the voice of your words, and was wroth, and swore, saying, [35] <dq>‘Not one of these men of this evil generation shall see that good land of which <dn>I</dn> swore to give to your fathers,</dq> [36] <dq>‘except Kaleḇ son of Yephunneh – he shall see it, and to him and his children <dn>I</dn> give the land on which he walked, because he followed <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> completely.’</dq> [37] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was also enraged with me for your sakes, saying, <dq>‘You do not go in there either.</dq> [38] <dq>‘Yehoshua son of Nun, who stands before you, he shall go in there. Strengthen him, for he shall cause Yisra’ĕl to inherit it.</dq> [39] <dq>‘And your little ones and your children, who you say are for a prey, who today have no knowledge of good and evil, they shall go in there. And to them <dn>I</dn> give it, and they possess it.</dq> [40] <dq>‘But you, turn and take your journey into the wilderness by the way of the Sea of Reeds.’</dq> [41] “Then you answered and said to me, ‘We have sinned against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. We ourselves are going up, and we shall fight, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> commanded us.’ And when every one of you had girded on his weapons of battle, you were ready to go up into the mountain. [42] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to me, <dq>‘Say to them, “Do not go up nor fight, for <dn>I</dn> am not in your midst, lest you be smitten before your enemies.” ’</dq> [43] “So I spoke to you, but you would not listen and rebelled against the mouth of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and were so proud that you went up into the mountain. [44] “And the Amorites who dwelt in that mountain came out against you and chased you as bees do, and drove you back from Sĕ’ir to Ḥormah. [45] “And you returned and wept before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, but <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> would not listen to your voice nor give ear to you. [46] “So you dwelt in Qaḏĕsh many days, according to the days that you dwelt there.”

readings.title: The Detour through the Wilderness
readings.subtitle: Sparing the Sons of Ěsaw and Mo’aḇ
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 2:1] “Then we turned and took our journey into the wilderness by the way of the Sea of Reeds, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to me, and we went round Mount Sĕ’ir many days. [2] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to me, saying, [3] <dq>‘You have gone round this mountain long enough, turn northward.</dq> [4] <dq>‘And command the people, saying, “You are about to pass through the border of your brothers, the descendants of Ěsaw, who live in Sĕ’ir, and they are afraid of you. So be very careful.</dq> [5] <dq>“Do not strive with them, for <dn>I</dn> do not give you any of their land, no, not so much as a footstep, because <dn>I</dn> have given Mount Sĕ’ir to Ěsaw as a possession.</dq> [6] <dq>“Buy food from them with silver, and eat; and also buy water from them with silver, and drink.</dq> [7] <dq>“For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has blessed you in all the work of your hand. <dn>He</dn> knows your journeying through this great wilderness. These forty years <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has been with you, you have lacked not a word.” ’</dq> [8] “And when we passed beyond our brothers, the descendants of Ěsaw who dwelt in Sĕ’ir, away from the way of the desert plain, away from Ělath and Etsyon Geḇer, we turned and passed by the way of the Wilderness of Mo’aḇ. [9] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to me, <dq>‘Do not distress Mo’aḇ, nor strive with them in battle, for <dn>I</dn> do not give you any of their land as a possession, because <dn>I</dn> have given Ar to the descendants of Lot as a possession.’</dq> [10] (The Ěmites had dwelt there in the past, a people as great and numerous and tall as the Anaqim. [11] They were also reckoned as Repha’im, like the Anaqim, but the Mo’aḇites call them Ěmites. [12] And the Ḥorites had formerly dwelt in Sĕ’ir, but the descendants of Ěsaw dispossessed them and destroyed them from before them, and dwelt in their place, as Yisra’ĕl did to the land of his possession which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gave to them.) [13] <dq>‘Now rise up and pass over the wadi Zereḏ.’</dq> So we passed over the wadi Zereḏ. [14] “And the time we took to come from Qaḏĕsh Barnĕa until we passed over the wadi Zereḏ was thirty-eight years, until all the generation of the men of battle was consumed from the midst of the camp, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had sworn to them. [15] “And also the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was against them, to destroy them from the midst of the camp, until they were consumed. [16] “And it came to be, when all the men of battle had finally perished from among the people, [17] that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to me, saying, [18] <dq>‘Today you are to pass over at Ar, the border of Mo’aḇ.</dq> [19] <dq>‘And when you come near the front of the children of Ammon, do not distress them nor strive with them, for <dn>I</dn> do not give you any of the land of the children of Ammon as a possession, because <dn>I</dn> have given it to the descendants of Lot as a possession.’</dq> [20] (That also was reckoned as a land of Repha’im. Repha’im had dwelt there in the past, but the Ammonites call them Zamzummim, [21] a people as great and numerous and tall as the Anaqim. But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> destroyed them before them, and they dispossessed them and dwelt in their place, [22] as <dn>He</dn> had done for the descendants of Ěsaw, who dwelt in Sĕ’ir, when <dn>He</dn> destroyed the Ḥorites from before them. And they dispossessed them and dwelt in their place, even to this day. [23] And the Avvim, who dwelt in villages as far as Azzah – the Kaphtorim, who came from Kaphtor, destroyed them and dwelt in their place.) [24] <dq>‘Rise up, take your journey, and pass over the wadi Arnon. See, <dn>I</dn> have given into your hand Siḥon the Amorite, sovereign of H_eshbon, and his land. Begin to possess it, and strive with him in battle.</dq> [25] <dq>‘This day <dn>I</dn> begin to put the dread and fear of you upon the peoples under all the heavens, who, when they hear the report of you, shall tremble and shake because of you.’</dq>”

readings.title: The Conquest of Siḥon
readings.subtitle: The First Victory East of the Yardĕn
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 2:26] “And I sent messengers from the Wilderness of Qeḏĕmoth to Siḥon sovereign of Ḥeshbon, with words of peace, saying, [27] ‘Let me pass through your land. I go only by the way, turning neither to the right nor to the left. [28] ‘Sell me food for silver, and I shall eat; and give me water for silver, and I shall drink. Only let me pass through on foot, [29] ‘as the descendants of Ěsaw who dwell in Sĕ’ir and the Mo’aḇites who dwell in Ar did for me, until I pass over the Yardĕn into the land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving us.’ [30] “But Siḥon sovereign of Ḥeshbon would not let us pass through him, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> hardened his spirit and made his heart stubborn, to give him into your hand, as it is today. [31] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to me, <dq>‘See, <dn>I</dn> have begun to deliver Siḥon and his land over to you. Begin to possess, so as to possess his land.’</dq> [32] “And Siḥon and all his people came out against us to battle at Yahats. [33] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> delivered him over to us, and we smote him and his sons and all his people. [34] “And we took all his cities at that time, and we put under the ban the men, and the women, and the little ones of every city. We left no survivor. [35] “Only the livestock we took as plunder for ourselves, and the spoil of the cities which we took. [36] “From Aro’ĕr, which is on the edge of the wadi Arnon, and the city that is in the wadi, as far as Gil’aḏ, there was not one city too high for us. <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> delivered all over to us. [37] “Only to the land of the children of Ammon you did not come near, all along the wadi Yabbog̱, and the cities of the mountains, and all that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> had forbidden us.”

readings.title: The Overthrow of Og̱
readings.subtitle: The Giant of Bashan
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 3:1] “Then we turned and went up the way to Bashan. And Og̱ sovereign of Bashan came out against us, he and all his people, to battle at Edre’i. [2] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to me, <dq>‘Do not fear him, for <dn>I</dn> have given him and all his people and his land into your hand. And you shall do to him as you did to Siḥon sovereign of the Amorites, who dwelt at Ḥeshbon.’</dq> [3] “So <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> also delivered Og̱ sovereign of Bashan and all his people into our hands, and we smote him until no survivor was left to him. [4] “And we took all his cities at that time. There was not a city which we did not take from them: sixty cities, all the region of Argoḇ, the reign of Og̱ in Bashan. [5] “All these cities were walled with high walls, gates and bars, besides a great many unwalled towns. [6] “And we put them under the ban, as we did to Siḥon sovereign of Ḥeshbon, putting under the ban the men, women, and little ones of every city. [7] “But all the livestock and the spoil of the cities we took as plunder for ourselves. [8] “And at that time we took the land out of the hand of the two sovereigns of the Amorites that were beyond the Yardĕn, from the wadi Arnon to Mount Ḥermon [9] (Sidonians call Ḥermon, Siryon, and the Amorites call it Senir), [10] all the cities of the plain, all Gil’aḏ, and all Bashan, as far as Saleḵah and Edre’i, cities of the reign of Og̱ in Bashan. [11] “For only Og̱ sovereign of Bashan was left of the remnant of the Repha’im. See, his bedstead was an iron bedstead. Is it not in Rabbah of the children of Ammon? Nine cubits is its length and four cubits its width, according to the cubit of a man.”

readings.title: Assigning the Transjordan
readings.subtitle: A Place for the Livestock
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 3:12] “And this land, which we possessed at that time, from Aro’ĕr, which is by the wadi Arnon, and half the mountains of Gil’aḏ and its cities, I gave to the Re’uḇĕnites and to the Gaḏites. [13] “And the rest of Gil’aḏ, and all Bashan, the reign of Og̱, I gave to half the tribe of Menashshĕh. All the region of Argoḇ, with all Bashan, was called the land of Repha’im. [14] “Ya’ir son of Menashshĕh took all the region of Argoḇ, as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Ma’aḵathites, and called them after his own name, Bashan Ḥawwoth Ya’ir, to this day. [15] “And I gave Gil’aḏ to Maḵir. [16] “And to the Re’uḇĕnites and to the Gaḏites I gave from Gil’aḏ as far as the wadi Arnon, the middle of the wadi as the border, as far as the wadi Yabbog̱, the border of the children of Ammon, [17] and the desert plain, with the Yardĕn as the border, from Kinnereth as far as the Sea of the Araḇah, the Salt Sea, below the slopes of Pisgah eastward. [18] “And I commanded you at that time, saying, <dq>‘<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has given you this land to possess. All you sons of might, pass over armed before your brothers, the children of Yisra’ĕl.</dq> [19] <dq>‘Only your wives, and your little ones, and your livestock – I know that you have much livestock – shall stay in your cities which <dn>I</dn> have given you,</dq> [20] <dq>‘until <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has given rest to your brothers as to you, and they also possess the land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving them beyond the Yardĕn. Then you shall each return to his possession which <dn>I</dn> have given you.’</dq>”
